title: Find a target pair
summary: A checkout system stores each item price as an integer. Given an array of values and a target, return the indices of two different entries whose values add to the target. Use the first valid pair in index order, and return an empty array when no pair exists.
requirements: Accept nums (an array of integers) and target (an integer). Return [left, right], where left < right and nums[left] + nums[right] equals target.
If several pairs work, return the pair with the smallest right index; if tied, use the smallest left index.
Return [] when no pair exists. You cannot reuse the same position twice.
Do not change nums. Negative numbers, zero, and duplicate values are allowed.
Inputs contain at most 10,000 numbers, each between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000. Aim for O(n) time using a hash map.
hints: For each value, the other value you need is target minus the current value.
Store previously seen values and their indices in a Map. Check for the complement before adding the current position.
Keep the first index stored for a value. Scanning right indices from left to right then returns the required pair.

tests.name: Keeps the earliest index for duplicates
Returns empty when no pair exists
